name: Cartouche for SideStore
subtitle: Install Cartouche with your SideStore
description: The source to add to your own SideStore to install Cartouche without a computer. It lists Cartouche and nothing else: Cartouche never lists, hosts or downloads games. When SideStore asks about Cartouche's app extensions, keep them on the main profile.

apps.name: Cartouche
apps.subtitle: Play your own games built with nxnative
apps.localizedDescription: Cartouche runs the games you build with nxnative from your own copies, renews itself without a computer, and gives them Increased Memory Limit. It never downloads a game.

versions.localizedDescription:
Cartouche 0.17.0 adds mods for each game, keeps your music playing, pauses a game when its controller disconnects, lets your Mac renew Cartouche and carries every profile of a game with its saves.

- Mods: on a game's sheet, Mods adds one from Files, as its folder or its ZIP, turns each on or off and sets their order, the one higher up winning. A mod that changes the game's code too is left out, with why. On your iPhone, iPad and Mac. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Home filter: with games installed and games not installed yet, on your Mac, in a games folder or in Cartouche Cloud, a menu beside My library shows All, Installed or Not installed, and L and R change it with a controller. Cartouche keeps your choice. Also on your Mac. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Saves folder: once your first game is over, while its saves are on this iPhone alone, the home offers to keep them safe in a folder on iCloud Drive, your Mac or a NAS: a tap opens Storage, and its × takes it off for good. A reinstall then loses nothing. Also on your Mac. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Your music while playing: turn on Keep other apps’ sound, in System › While a game runs, and the music or podcast you play in another app goes on under the game's sound, from the game's next start. Off until you turn it on. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Controller lost: a game pauses when its last controller disconnects. 3 seconds later the console comes back and says so, and connecting a controller again brings the game back. A game you play on the screen alone never pauses; System › While a game runs turns it off. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Renewed by your Mac: signed in once on the iPhone page of Cartouche for Mac, your Mac renews Cartouche on your iPhone in its last two days, by the cable or on your Wi-Fi, with no reinstall, and Cartouche shows its new date. Your password goes to Apple alone, and is asked again only once Apple ends the session. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Reinstalled by your Mac: when Cartouche's certificate is gone from your Apple Account, your Mac installs the newest Cartouche over it, with its games and saves: by itself once it expires, or at once with Reinstall on the iPhone page of Cartouche for Mac. It never revokes a certificate. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Every profile and shader: the saves of a game's players 2 to 8 now go and come with the first's, on your iPhone, iPad and Mac, each with the room the game made for it. A save from JKSV keeps the room it had on your console. And the shaders a game prepared come back after a reinstall, a reset or on another device, with those your other devices prepared, so its first games stutter less. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Back to the start: Put back a copy, on a game's sheet, now also lists the copies the game keeps on this iPhone of the saves each session starts from, even without a saves folder. If a game or a mod went wrong, put back the copy of its start; the saves it replaces are kept too. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Settings in your language: every setting nxnative gives a game now reads in your language, Rotation, Texture filtering and Microphone among them. Rotation now locks a game sideways or upright behind Cartouche's console too, as soon as you pick it in the game's menu. A game that has Polish or Thai starts in it on an iPhone set to it. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Prompts in your language: the prompt that waits for more players and the four labels of nxnative's menu over a game now read in Cartouche's language on your iPhone too, as on the Mac, behind the console or in Cartouche's place. The settings in that menu keep nxnative's English names. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Out of room: when a game stops because your iPhone ran out of room for the memory it keeps in files while it plays, Cartouche now says so and how much was free, instead of only saying the game closed. Before a start that may end that way, it warns you, with Play anyway. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Pipelines for your GPU: Cartouche now tells your Mac your iPhone's GPU, so that a game that bundles its Metal 4 pipelines, such as Breath of the Wild, is built with them for your iPhone too and no longer prepares them for minutes at its first start. Needs Cartouche for Mac 0.9.0, and a new build of the game. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Converted builds: on an iPhone whose GPU reads no BC textures, the question before an install now reads the game's build first: a build that converts its textures, from your Mac, a games folder or Cartouche Cloud, installs at once, and a Cartouche Cloud game built from nxnative-nobc says so on its sheet. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- iPhone 11 to 15: on an iPhone whose GPU reads no BC textures, the question before an install and System now say that Cartouche Cloud builds its games from nxnative-nobc too, for a game you send for an iPhone 11 to 15. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- LocalDevVPN port: signing in, renewing and updating no longer stop at once when another service of your iPhone answers at the port Cartouche reaches it at through LocalDevVPN: Cartouche looks for the right port again. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Certificate import: Import signing certificate opens the same Files picker as Import my copy, for the certificate (.p12) and its profile, so that the certificate you tap there comes back to the page, on iOS 27.3 too. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Install screen: while a game installs from your Mac on Wi-Fi, its screen no longer says cable because your iPhone was plugged in to the Mac for something else.

Cartouche 0.16.2 can bring a game of your NAS through your Mac and its cable, when the Mac is on Ethernet.

- NAS through your Mac: with the iPhone plugged into your Mac by a cable, and the Mac on Ethernet, the Mac reads the game on the NAS and passes it on through the cable, instead of the iPhone's Wi-Fi, and the install screen says By cable, through the Mac. On the Mac's Wi-Fi, the iPhone reads the NAS itself, as before. Needs Cartouche 0.8.1 or later on your Mac, which updates itself. Not tried with a real Mac and NAS yet.

Cartouche 0.16.1 installs again from your own SideStore: it asks your SideStore for the pairing file, and a copy without its app group says what to do.

- Your own SideStore: in 0.16.0, Cartouche asked its own built-in SideStore for the pairing file instead of yours; it asks yours again. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Without its app group: a copy of the IPA for SideStore installed without its app group, as some signing apps do, no longer asks for your Apple ID only to fail; it says so, and offers the IPA for your own certificate or the Installer instead. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.

Cartouche 0.16.0 speaks Spanish and German, installs from your own SideStore without a computer, guides you through the nightly renewal, reads several games folders, reaches your Mac by cable and sends your saves while you play.

- Spanish and German: Cartouche now speaks Spanish and German besides English and French, on the iPhone, the iPad and the Mac, and follows your device's language as before. The guides stay in English and French. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Your own SideStore: you can now install Cartouche with the SideStore you already have, no computer needed. Add the source source.cartouche.cloud to your SideStore and install Cartouche from it, keeping its extensions on the main profile. Its setup asks your SideStore for the pairing file, takes its certificate when you sign in with the same Apple ID, then reinstalls Cartouche once to get Increased Memory Limit. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Renew every night: the setup's last step guides you through the Shortcuts automation that renews Cartouche every night, and Cartouche now sees each of its runs: the step and System say whether it is to make, on, failed (no LocalDevVPN, interrupted, or SideStore's error) or no longer running. Once your first game is installed, the home reminds you of it until you make it or take the reminder off, and Cartouche asks to warn you before its signature expires. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Expired Apple session: when Apple says the session Cartouche renews with has expired, Cartouche signs in again by itself once and renews itself; otherwise the System page asks you to sign in again, and Cartouche no longer retries every six hours. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Your first game: with no game yet, How to get a game, beside Import my copy on the home and on a game's sheet, opens the guide. With no Mac, its third step now offers Cartouche Cloud, which builds your game for you, and I have my own IPAs already, which opens Files; linked to Cartouche Cloud, its last step installs the game it built, and the guide opens on the step left. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Several games folders: in Storage, Add another games folder reads another folder too, on any of your servers. A game in several shows once and installs from a folder whose server answers, so a game on your NAS that your Google Drive also holds installs away from home; its sheet says where the other copies are, and an install whose server does not answer goes on from the next copy. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Folders from the Mac: the games folders and the saves folder can now be changed on your Mac's console too, on one of your connections, and your iPhone takes them the next time Cartouche opens, the folder chosen last winning on either side. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Mac by cable: plugged into your Mac with a cable, the iPhone reaches Cartouche on your Mac and installs your games from it without Wi-Fi; Wi-Fi takes over again once unplugged. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Install speed: while a game installs from your Mac or a NAS, its screen shows how it comes (cable, Tailscale, or the Mac's Wi-Fi band) and how fast, with a tip when the Mac is on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi or the game comes slowly. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Saves sent while playing: a game behind the console sends its saves to your saves folder a few seconds after each save, not only after the game; offline, they still go after it. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- iCloud backup: the games Cartouche installs no longer go into your iPhone's backup, iCloud's or a computer's, as they install again from your storage; their saves still do. Games already installed leave it the first time this version opens. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Other installed apps: an IPA you install that is not an nxnative game is now on the System page, under Other installed apps, to open or uninstall; Cartouche no longer sends you to an Apps tab that does not exist. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- iPhones without BC: on an iPhone whose GPU reads no BC textures (iPhone 11 to 15), System and the question before an install now say that Cartouche on your Mac builds its games from nxnative-nobc, a separate fork of nxnative that converts those textures, once the two are paired. A game drawn with Vulkan whose build converts them is no longer Not supported on this iPhone, and a converted game still on your Mac or in a games folder no longer shows the warning before its install: its sheet says Textures converted for this GPU by this game's build. Games drawn with OpenGL keep the warning. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Game sheet memory: with Keep Cartouche open behind the game off, a game's sheet now counts the 8 GB Game Mode gives Cartouche a moment after it opens, on iPhones with 12 GB. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Cartouche Cloud games: a game you built and already installed now says On this iPhone instead of Install, and the Cloud page shows each game's cover and the four phases of its build as it runs. Not tried on a real iPhone yet.
- Cartouche on the Mac: the Mac's app is now called Cartouche, as on the iPhone, and the Storage page says Add your Mac.
